name: Selegiline
lead: Selegiline, also called deprenyl, is a selective, irreversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B), an enzyme that breaks down dopamine. It is prescribed mainly as an add-on for Parkinson's disease, and a transdermal patch form is approved for depression [1][14].

In looksmaxxing, biohacking and nootropic circles it is discussed as a dopamine-supporting, recovery and longevity compound. Proponents link higher dopamine signalling to better mood, drive and focus, and they connect these to training consistency, self-care and a more youthful presentation. The chain from selegiline to appearance is therefore indirect: mood and motivation, then habits such as lifting and sleep, then physique and skin. These are claims from communities; the published research is in medical conditions rather than appearance [3].

The US label describes it as an adjunct to levodopa/carbidopa in Parkinson's patients whose response has deteriorated [4]. A 2022 review of cognitive enhancers lists selegiline among drugs used by healthy people, noting that effects in healthy individuals are uncertain and reported improvements temporary [3].

More consistent training and self-care, and in turn physique and presentation
angle.text: Selegiline is used by some people to support dopamine, mood and focus, which they say helps them stay consistent with training and self-care. Any link to appearance is through this indirect chain [3].

paras: The US label indicates selegiline tablets as an adjunct in Parkinson's patients on levodopa/carbidopa who show a deteriorating response; the label notes no controlled-study evidence of benefit without levodopa [4]. The transdermal form, Emsam, is approved for major depressive disorder [1]. Parkinson's treatment reviews cover its place among motor-symptom therapies [9].

Wikipedia reports that oral and orally disintegrating forms are usually added to levodopa to reduce the levodopa dose needed, and that selegiline's neuroprotective effect is disputed [14]. For depression, the patch is licensed while oral use is off-label; a 2023 meta-analysis cited by Wikipedia found benefit over placebo, with evidence quality rated very low for oral use and low to moderate for the patch [14]. The patch is underused largely because of its cost [14]. Research has also explored it in narcolepsy, Alzheimer's disease and substance dependence [5][10][12][13].

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and nootropic communities
paras: Selegiline is discussed as a cognitive enhancer and as an anti-aging agent. A review of smart drugs in healthy individuals includes it, describing users' enthusiastic anecdotal reports alongside uncertain efficacy in non-impaired brains [3].

At doses used for Parkinson's disease, selegiline selectively and irreversibly inhibits MAO-B, which raises dopamine in the brain; at higher doses selectivity falls and MAO-A is also inhibited, raising serotonin and norepinephrine [1][14]. Wikipedia describes it as also enhancing impulse-driven release of dopamine and norepinephrine, and notes that its metabolites include levomethamphetamine and levoamphetamine, which act as norepinephrine releasers [14]. Reviews of MAO-A and MAO-B inhibitors in psychiatry and neurology cover the class [15].

Wikipedia lists serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs and tyramine-related hypertensive reactions as the dangerous interactions, with higher risk at high oral doses and lower risk with the orally disintegrating tablet and patch [14]. The label warns that selectivity may not be absolute and that hypertensive reactions with tyramine-rich foods have been reported rarely at recommended doses [4].

The label cautions against exceeding recommended daily doses because of non-selective MAO inhibition risks [4]. Drug interactions are a major consideration for MAO inhibitors, and the label lists pregnancy category C [4].

Wikipedia lists insomnia, dry mouth, dizziness and anxiety as common effects, orthostatic hypotension especially at the start and in older adults, rare impulse-control problems, and a boxed warning for suicidality on the patch [14]. It states that selegiline is not a controlled substance in most countries, with Japan an exception, and that no misuse potential or dependence liability is known [14].

Wikipedia reports that Zoltan Ecseri, Jozsef Knoll and colleagues at Chinoin in Hungary studied deprenyl as an antidepressant in the early 1960s, after which its purified levorotatory enantiomer, selegiline, was developed [14][1]. It was first used medically for Parkinson's in Hungary in 1977, approved in the UK in 1982 and in the US in 1989 [14]. The orally disintegrating tablet was approved in the US in 2006 and in the EU in 2010, and the patch for depression was introduced in the US in 2006 [14].
A 1989 Science paper examined deprenyl's effect on the natural history of Parkinson's disease [8].

Studies include a 1997 randomized trial of selegiline and vitamin E in 341 patients with moderately severe Alzheimer's disease [5], a 1984 open trial in 17 patients with atypical depression, 10 of whom responded [6], a trial in narcolepsy [10], and registered trials in Parkinson's daytime sleepiness [11], cocaine dependence [12], smoking cessation [13] and others. A review of cognitive enhancers found efficacy in healthy people uncertain [3]. No studies found for cosmetic or appearance outcomes. A study compared switching Parkinson's patients from selegiline to the orally disintegrating Zelapar formulation [16]. Trials in Parkinson's disease daytime sleepiness enrolled 141 participants [11], and a smoking cessation study 101 [13].

lore.intro: Selegiline is discussed in nootropic and anti-aging corners of enthusiast communities as a dopamine-supporting compound; it is less central to looksmaxxing forums than to biohacking.

claims.claim: It boosts motivation, focus and mood in healthy people.
claims.believers: Users describe sharper drive and mood, which they tie to consistent training.
claims.experts: A 2022 review says efficacy in healthy individuals is uncertain and any improvement temporary [3].

claims.claim: It slows aging and extends lifespan.
claims.believers: Proponents cite early animal-lifespan work and neuroprotection claims.
claims.experts: Trials in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's have examined disease progression [5][8]; no study has tested aging appearance.

card.summary: A prescription MAO-B inhibitor that raises brain dopamine; some people use it for mood, drive and recovery, and it is also discussed as a nootropic.
card.note: Prescription drug; MAO inhibition carries serious drug and food interaction cautions.

quick.overview:
Selegiline is a prescription drug that blocks the MAO-B enzyme, letting dopamine last longer in the brain. It is used for Parkinson's disease, and a patch form for depression.

Some people in nootropic and biohacking communities use it hoping for better mood, focus and drive, which they link to training and self-care.
quick.mechanism: It irreversibly inhibits MAO-B, reducing dopamine breakdown; at higher doses it also inhibits MAO-A [1].
quick.risks: Labelling warns about exceeding recommended doses and about interactions, including rare hypertensive reactions with tyramine-rich foods [4]. It is prescription-only.
